extraction.name: Introduction to the CoNLL-2003 Shared Task: Language-Independent Named Entity Recognition
extraction.description: Paper describing the CoNLL-2003 shared task for language-independent named entity recognition, including dataset sources, preprocessing, annotation, evaluation, participating systems, and results for English and German.
extraction.creator: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang; Fien De Meulder
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The CoNLL-2003 named entity data consists of eight files covering English and German, with training, development, test, and unannotated data for each language. English data was taken from the Reuters Corpus; German data was taken from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus, specifically texts from the German newspaper Frankfurter Rundshau. The paper also states that named entity tagging of the English and German training, development, and test data was done by hand at the University of Antwerp.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis; Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: English raw data: Reuters news stories from the Reuters Corpus, between August 1996 and August 1997. German raw data: texts from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus, extracted from the German newspaper Frankfurter Rundshau, with raw data taken from September to December 1992.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: English training/development data from the end of August 1996; English test data from December 1996; German training/development/test data from articles written in one week at the end of August 1992.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For all data, a tokenizer, part-of-speech tagger, and chunker were applied to the raw data. English data was tagged and chunked by the memory-based MBT tagger. German data was lemmatized, tagged, and chunked by the decision tree tagger Treetagger. The data files were formatted with one word per line and empty lines for sentence boundaries.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Named entity tagging of English and German training, development, and test data was done by hand at the University of Antwerp. Mostly MUC conventions were followed. An extra named entity category called MISC was added to denote names not already in the other categories.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The tagging scheme used was the IOB scheme. The paper notes that named entities are non-recursive and non-overlapping, and when a named entity is embedded in another named entity, usually only the top level entity has been annotated.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Persons, organizations, locations, and miscellaneous named entities are annotated; the paper does not describe collection of sensitive human attributes such as gender, age, socio-economic status, or language.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper frames named entity recognition as an important task of information extraction systems and discusses shared-task evaluation for advancing language-independent NER.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that the English data came from Reuters news stories and the German data from a German newspaper corpus, which may bias the dataset toward news text.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper states that the challenge was to incorporate unannotated data in the learning process and that the resources used by some systems, such as gazetteers and externally trained named entity systems, still require a lot of manual work. It also notes that systems tuned on development data were separated from test data to avoid tuning to the test set.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, development/tuning, and testing for named entity recognition systems; the shared task also encouraged use of unannotated data for learning.
